title: Evaluating a Reusable Container Trial
transcript:
We've finished the first week of observations at the takeaway shops. More customers chose reusable containers at the smaller shop, but I don't think we can conclude that its reminder poster was more effective.
Why not? The two shops agreed to display different posters, so I expected us to compare the proportion of customers choosing the returnable option. Was there a problem with how the posters were displayed?
The display was fine, but the smaller shop serves many regular customers. Staff recognise them and often explain the scheme during conversation. At the larger shop, people queue quickly and may never speak to the same employee twice.
Then the customer mix and staff interaction could explain the difference. We need to record those factors. Did both shops charge the same deposit for taking a reusable container away?
Yes. The deposit was identical and fully returned when the container came back. However, one shop accepted returns at a separate counter, while the other required people to join the food queue even if they weren't buying lunch.
That could affect returns more than initial participation. Perhaps we should separate the decision to take a container from the decision to bring it back. Our current spreadsheet puts both into one success measure.
Agreed. We also need a way to track individual containers without collecting customers' names. Each container already has a barcode, so staff could scan it when it leaves and when it returns.
That would let us measure how long containers stay out and how many complete several cycles. We should ask whether the shops can export those records consistently, rather than assume their systems work in the same way.
There is another cost: cleaning. One manager said the washing process takes longer when lids arrive separately. We could observe the process and record staff time, but we'd need permission first.
Let's include that, along with damaged or missing containers. A high return rate does not necessarily mean the scheme is cheap to operate. The final report should discuss practical costs as well as customer participation.
Should we recommend the better-performing poster after the trial, or would that claim be too strong given the differences between the two shops? The business partners will probably want a simple recommendation.
We can recommend a follow-up trial that swaps the posters between shops while keeping the other procedures stable. If the pattern changes with the poster, that would be stronger evidence. For now, we should report the differences without assigning them to one cause.

questions.prompt: Both shops charge the same refundable ____.
questions.explanation: 两店押金相同且归还容器时全额退回。

questions.prompt: Why should taking and returning a container be measured separately?
options: They may be influenced by different procedures
Only the first decision matters to the shops
questions.answer: They may be influenced by different procedures
questions.explanation: 取用和归还可能分别受宣传与退回流程等不同因素影响。

questions.prompt: Each container has a ____ that can be scanned.
questions.explanation: 已有条码可跟踪容器循环，不必记录顾客姓名。

questions.prompt: The washing process takes longer when ____ arrive separately.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说盖子单独送达时，清洗过程会更耗时。

questions.prompt: What follow-up trial do the students suggest?
options: Swapping the posters while other procedures stay stable
Closing the busier shop during observations
questions.answer: Swapping the posters while other procedures stay stable
questions.explanation: 交换海报并稳定其他流程，能更好判断海报作用。
